result.topic_en: Scholion 2 shows that the quotient $(p^7-q^7)/(p-q)$ can be written in the form $ff+7gg$, so for primes of the form $7n+1$ the number $-7$ always appears among the quadratic residues, confirming an earlier conjecture.
result.transcription:
PER NVMEROS PRIMOS. 135
reperiri $+5$, quod cum coniectura ante allata congruit.

Scholion 2.

97. Simili modo si poteſtates ſeptimae per numerum primum $7n+1$ diuidantur, dabuntur huiusmodi formae $p^7-q^7$ ſeu $p^6+p^5q+p^4q^2+p^3q^3$ $+p^2q^4+pq^5+q^6$ per eum diuiſibiles; haec vero expreſſio reducitur ad hanc formam:
$(p^3+\tfrac{1}{2}ppq-\tfrac{1}{2}pqq-q^3)^2+7(\tfrac{1}{2}ppq+\tfrac{1}{2}pqq)^2.$
Vnde ſemper numeri huius formae $ff+7gg$ exhiberi poſſunt per numerum primum $7n+1$ diuiſibiles. Ex quo ſequitur ſi omnia quadrata per numerum primum formae $7n+1$ diuidantur inter reſidua certe repertum iri $-7$, quo etiam coniectura ſupra data confirmatur.

NOVA

items.quote: reperiri $+5$, quod cum coniectura ante allata congruit.
items.english: ...that $+5$ is found, which agrees with the conjecture brought forward earlier.

items.quote:
haec vero expreſſio reducitur ad hanc formam:
$(p^3+\tfrac{1}{2}ppq-\tfrac{1}{2}pqq-q^3)^2+7(\tfrac{1}{2}ppq+\tfrac{1}{2}pqq)^2.$
items.english: This expression reduces to the form $(p^3+\tfrac12 p^2q-\tfrac12 pq^2-q^3)^2+7(\tfrac12 p^2q+\tfrac12 pq^2)^2$.

items.quote: Ex quo ſequitur ſi omnia quadrata per numerum primum formae $7n+1$ diuidantur inter reſidua certe repertum iri $-7$, quo etiam coniectura ſupra data confirmatur.
items.english: From this it follows that if all squares are divided by a prime number of the form $7n+1$, $-7$ will certainly be found among the residues, by which the conjecture given above is also confirmed.
